gloss: running the full distance; completing a course

definitions.gloss: running the full distance; covering the entire course
definitions.explanation: Successfully running or traveling the entire length of a route or course. Used for races, road trips, and challenging journeys. Implies endurance and accomplishment.

examples.japanese: フルマラソンを{走破|そうは}した。
{全|ぜん}コースを{三時間|さんじかん}で{走破|そうは}した。
examples.english: I covered the entire course in three hours.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{日本列島|にほんれっとう}を{自転車|じてんしゃ}で{縦断|じゅうだん}{走破|そうは}するという{挑戦|ちょうせん}に{成功|せいこう}した。
examples.english: He succeeded in his challenge to cycle the entire length of the Japanese archipelago.

notes:
Composed of {走|そう} (run) + {破|は} (break through). The {破|は} component conveys the sense of pushing through to completion despite difficulty. Primarily used in sports and travel contexts where completing a long or challenging distance is an achievement.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {走破|そうは}する: to run/cover the full distance
- {全|ぜん}コースを{走破|そうは}する: to complete the entire course
- {走破|そうは}{距離|きょり}: distance covered
- {走破|そうは}{時間|じかん}: completion time
- {走破|そうは}{記録|きろく}: course completion record

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {完走|かんそう}: finishing a race — emphasizes completing the race, especially without dropping out
- {踏破|とうは}: traversing on foot — used for hiking or walking through difficult terrain
- {縦断|じゅうだん}: traveling the full length — traversing something from end to end (north-south or top-bottom)
